answer: Propose tidal-gauge attestation at a wharf. Each miner claims one berth on a basalt wharf and bonds a small stake to it; the berth's sensor is keyed to that basalt structure, so one sensor serves one identity. At a tide height from the tide table, the network opens a short window for the miner to submit the gauge reading, signed by the sensor. Readings are checked against the tide curve and neighboring berths, so forgery stands out. A Sybil operator cannot clone berths without buying wharf hardware and staking each one, making mass identities costly, while honest miners are refunded.
